# Post hoc {#sec-posthoc}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    p_i \leq \frac{\alpha}{m}
$${#eq-bonferroni}

$$
    p_k \leq \frac{\alpha}{ m + 1 - k}
$${#eq-holm}
$$
    p_i \leq 1 - (1 - \alpha)^{1/m}
$${#eq-sidak}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Post-hoc Tests: Bonferroni, Holm, and FDR Corrections"
#| label: fig-posthoc-test

# Create the same sample data as in chap_anova
set.seed(789)
group_a <- rnorm(30, mean = 50, sd = 5)
group_b <- rnorm(30, mean = 55, sd = 5)
group_c <- rnorm(30, mean = 52, sd = 5)

# Combine into a data frame
posthoc_data <- data.frame(
  values = c(group_a, group_b, group_c),
  group = rep(c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"), each = 30)
)

# First, run ANOVA to confirm significant differences
anova_model <- aov(values ~ group, data = posthoc_data)
print("ANOVA Results:")
print(summary(anova_model))

# Post-hoc Test 1: Bonferroni correction
print("\n========== Bonferroni Correction ==========")
posthoc_bonferroni <- pairwise.t.test(posthoc_data$values, posthoc_data$group,
                                       p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
print(posthoc_bonferroni)

# Post-hoc Test 2: Holm correction
print("\n========== Holm Correction ==========")
posthoc_holm <- pairwise.t.test(posthoc_data$values, posthoc_data$group,
                                p.adjust.method = "holm")
print(posthoc_holm)

# Post-hoc Test 3: FDR correction
print("\n========== FDR Correction ==========")
posthoc_fdr <- pairwise.t.test(posthoc_data$values, posthoc_data$group,
                                 p.adjust.method = "fdr")
print(posthoc_fdr)

# Summary comparison
print("\n========== Summary of Results ==========")
print("Bonferroni p-values:")
print(round(posthoc_bonferroni$p.value, 4))
print("\nHolm p-values:")
print(round(posthoc_holm$p.value, 4))
print("\nfdr p-values:")
print(round(posthoc_fdr$p.value, 4))

# Interpretation:
# Bonferroni: Most conservative, divides α by number of comparisons
# Holm: Less conservative than Bonferroni, adjusts stepwise
# Sidak: Similar to Bonferroni but slightly less conservative
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Post-hoc Comparison: P-value Adjustments"
#| label: fig-posthoc-pvalues

# Extract raw p-values and adjusted values for comparison
comparisons <- c("A vs B", "A vs C", "B vs C")

# Create a matrix of p-values for visualization
pval_matrix <- cbind(
  Bonferroni = as.vector(posthoc_bonferroni$p.value),
  Holm = as.vector(posthoc_holm$p.value),
  fdr = as.vector(posthoc_fdr$p.value)
)

# Set up 1x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Panel 1: Heatmap-style visualization of p-values
colors_heatmap <- function(x) {
  if(is.na(x)) return("white")
  if(x < 0.001) return("darkred")
  if(x < 0.01) return("red")
  if(x < 0.05) return("orange")
  return("lightgreen")
}

# Create a simple plot showing p-values
plot(NA, xlim = c(0.5, 3.5), ylim = c(0.5, 3.5),
     main = "Post-hoc P-values by Correction Method",
     xlab = "Correction Method",
     ylab = "Comparison",
     xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n")

axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = colnames(pval_matrix))
axis(2, at = 1:3, labels = comparisons)

# Add p-values as text with color coding
for(i in 1:3) {
  for(j in 1:3) {
    p_val <- pval_matrix[i, j]
    if(!is.na(p_val)) {
      color <- if(p_val < 0.05) "red" else "black"
      text(j, 4 - i, paste0(round(p_val, 4)),
           col = color, cex = 1.2, font = if(p_val < 0.05) 2 else 1)
    }
  }
}

# Add significance threshold line
abline(h = 1.5, v = 0.5, col = "gray", lty = 3)

# Panel 2: Bar plot of p-values for first comparison (A vs B)
pval_avb <- c(
  Bonferroni = pval_matrix[1, 1],
  Holm = pval_matrix[1, 2],
  fdr = pval_matrix[1, 3]
)

barplot(pval_avb,
        main = "P-values for Group A vs B Comparison",
        ylab = "Adjusted p-value",
        col = c("steelblue", "lightcoral", "lightgreen"),
        border = "black",
        lwd = 1.5,
        ylim = c(0, max(pval_avb) * 1.2))

# Add horizontal line at α = 0.05
abline(h = 0.05, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(1.5, 0.05 + 0.005, "α = 0.05", cex = 0.9, col = "red")

# Add values on bars
for(i in 1:3) {
  text(i * 1.2 - 0.6, pval_avb[i] + 0.01, round(pval_avb[i], 4),
       cex = 0.9, font = 2)
}

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
